newsitem.title: FRANCE: CCF RISES ON TAKEOVER/ACQUISITION HOPES.
newsitem.headline: CCF RISES ON TAKEOVER/ACQUISITION HOPES.

text.p: Shares in bank Credit Commercial de France (CCF) were up 3.85 percent at 334.40 francs at 1228 GMT on Thursday, boosted by comments from chairman Charles de Croisset on a possible large acquisition.
The stock earlier hit a year high at 331.80 francs and has gained around 32 percent since July 18.

Analysts said the rise was logical as the shares have underperformed the market for the last two years. Investors have criticised de Croisset for being too passive while the sector has been undergoing a shake-up.
An analyst at a non-French bank said that CCF "has a certain obligation to grow if it does not want to be eaten up".
De Croisset, apparently responding to his critics, said in an interview with the L'Agefi newspaper, that "there is no ideal size but an ideal profitability."
He did not, however, rule out "proceeding with major transactions aimed at external growth in France and abroad". He added, "We have the means".

Analyst Pascal Decque at CDC Bourse said, "CCF is being considered as a takeover target because of its insufficient size and dispersed shareholder base, but also as a predator thanks to its financial resources". CCF has the highest return on capital among French private banks, he said. It made a nine percent return last year.

Analysts are sceptical over CCF's international ambitions as it lacks the means to acquire a bank with a profitable foreign network. In France, they believe that CCF could buy the CIC bank, which the government is selling off as part of a rescue plan for its owner, ailing insurer Gan.
An offer by CCF for CIC could be well-received by the regional directors of CIC, said Patrick Leguil, research director at broker Transbourse.
"CCF has shown with previous acquisitions that it respects autonomy," he said, citing the example of the Banque de Savoie.

The two networks are seen as complementary as CCF has for several years sought out "clients with strong potential," he said. "They could keep CCF as an upmarket bank and have a more mass market network with CIC. In that case there would not be any duplication." he added.
Sector analysts do not exclude the possibility that CCF itself could be a takeover target, especially after the interest in France shown by Deutsche Bank and Dresdner Bank.
However, they added that CCF is valued at 22 times earnings, compared to 14 times for other French banks and its profitability is lower than that of German and British banks.
